main_text.l: illud unum utcunq; admonitos omnes
velim, ut summam & coronidem totius
hujus differtationis de Juramenti sensu
& interpretatione, magnopere ut ca-
veant, ne sibi nimium hac in re indulge-
ant; neu benigna nimis & laxa inter-
pretatione, dum cupiditatibus suis plus
æquo favent, Juramenti religionem mi-
nuant, & se perjurii periculo exponant.
Atque hæc de Formali Causa dicta suf-
ficiant.
SECT. XIV.
De Finali Causa paucula restant dic-
enda. Dubium Primum est, cum pro-
mittitur res ex se licita, sed aut mala in-
tentione, aut ob malum finem. Dicen-
dum primo, simpliciter illicitum esse pro-
mittere aliquid quantumvis in se licitum,
malo fine vel intentione. Ratio est, quia
cum quivis unus defectus in quolibet actu
humano sufficiat ad hoc, ut totus
actus sit malus, (Bonum enim ex causa
integra est, malum ex partiali:) tum
præcipue defectus ex parte finis, ut qui
in moralibus primas tenet partes; quo
fere putant id Christi dictum pertinere,

l.i: Si oculus tuus fuerit nequam, & totum

main_text.l: corpus tenebrosum erit. Dicendum fe-
{a} Si oculus tuus fuerit nequam, & totum corpus tenebrosum erit.

page.notes: The Latin note "Cafus 52" in the right margin is a side heading, read as "Causa 52" from the scan; the printed word may be "Cafus" (long s), so it is transcribed as "Causa" in the note text and should be checked. The scripture reference beside the foot line is marked "a" and is read as "Mat.6.13". The Greek-free text has no doubtful words; the foot line's italic runs across the column and is placed after the main text. The paragraph "Dicendum fe-" continues onto the next page.
